posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: Enterprise AI agents currently have access to an average of only 45% of organizational data, creating a significant bottleneck for autonomous decision-making.
Gartner predicts that AI agents will augment or automate 50% of business decisions by 2027, necessitating a shift away from legacy data infrastructure to maintain operational speed.
Data leaders, defined as organizations providing agents access to over 70% of their data, report higher success rates and greater ROI compared to laggards who provide access to 30% or less.

Effective agentic AI requires frictionless, real-time integration across structured and unstructured data sources, including supply chain and HR systems, which legacy architectures are currently failing to support.

posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 units in July, maintaining a streak above 30,000 units but leaving the company at only 39% of its 550,000-unit annual delivery target.
To meet its full-year goal, Xiaomi must significantly accelerate production to average nearly 67,000 units per month for the remainder of the year.
The company is pivoting toward the EREV segment with its new Sky Nomad series, which is priced aggressively against competitors like Li Auto and Huawei-backed Aito to drive volume.

posts.title: Chengdu Auto Show opens next week with nearly 120 brands, 1,600 vehicles
posts.summary:
The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show, China's first A-level event of the second half, will feature nearly 120 brands and 1,600 vehicles across 220,000 square meters.
Major manufacturers are using the event to debut key products, including BYD's D-segment flagship sedan, Huawei's new Maextro MPVs, and Xiaomi's extended-range SUV series.
The exhibition serves as a critical barometer for southwestern Chinese market demand and a strategic launchpad for automakers ahead of the peak autumn sales season.

posts.title: Hyundai's first Ioniq model for China to open pre-sales at Chengdu Auto Show
posts.summary:
The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Beijing Hyundai will open pre-sales for the Ioniq V at the Chengdu Auto Show, marking the first production model from its electric Ioniq brand in China.
The mid-size electric sedan features an 800-volt architecture, CATL battery packs, and an intelligent cockpit powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8295 chip.
Developed by Hyundai's China design center, the vehicle integrates local AI models like Baidu's Ernie Bot and ByteDance's Doubao, with plans for future global export.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to support linear drive optics in high-speed AI infrastructure.
Adopting linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50% by eliminating the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers within the optical module.
The new PHY IP addresses critical thermal and latency bottlenecks in dense AI racks, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G speeds and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO).

Measured performance data indicates that the IP meets or exceeds OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for TX VMA, jitter, and RX JTOL, ensuring interoperability in high-speed data center environments.
